scope: Final visible Draft, exact source/article/action bytes, rendered-link targets, fleet-runner stack ordering, daily-blog issue and subsequent run receipts, and current review registry/discovery state. Read-only review; no article revision or acceptance, finding disposition, action admission or settlement, readiness, merge, workflow dispatch, runtime, or scheduling authority.

findings.title: Two cross-repository links point at the wrong repositories
findings.location: Line 17 links core #578 to BookcaseDiscovery; line 32 links BookcaseDiscovery #28 to core.
findings.explanation: The visible anchors name the intended records, but their href targets swap repositories and lead to nonexistent or unrelated repository-number pairs.
findings.correction: Link the fleet-runner parent to core issue #578 and the compute-fleet plan to BookcaseDiscovery PR #28.

findings.title: The downstream fleet dependency order is reversed
findings.location: Lines 90, 98, 116 and 117 place #59 before #40 and #53 while saying no technical dependency remains.
findings.explanation: The PR bodies establish core #584 after #583, BookcaseDiscovery #40 after #584, #53 stacked on #40, and #59 stacked on #53. The article instead places #59 near the front and erases explicit stack-order dependencies.
findings.correction: State the downstream order as core #583 to #584 to BookcaseDiscovery #40 to #53 to #59, subject to recorded review and owner gates, and retain the technical ordering constraints.

findings.title: Issue 516 does not establish a current pipeline failure
findings.location: Lines 104, 116 and 119 call #516 a live daily-blog.yml failure and propose finding its unblock.
findings.explanation: Issue #516 records a November 1 failed run but no later status evidence. Subsequent scheduled run 41877544769 completed successfully and generated this article, so the open issue is not proof of a current failure.
findings.correction: Describe #516 as an open, stale alert whose current applicability is unverified; remove the live-failure and unblock premises unless a current failed receipt is linked.

findings.title: The single-session and reviewer-identity claim lacks a durable source binding
findings.location: Retained draft context at line 125 says all 28 PRs were reviewed in one session and no reviewer other than the owner is identified.
findings.explanation: Public PRs and commits prove the work and authenticated GitHub account, but do not expose a stable agent/chat session binding for all 28 reviews or establish that the shared login is the independent reviewer identity.
findings.correction: Omit the single-session and reviewer-identity claims, or link a durable public handoff record that proves them without relying on raw or private session transcripts.
